answer: Each new identity must harbor beneath a sponsor in a committed on-chain tree and post an ivory bond, a scarce deposit no operator can mint per clone. Proving one a sybil collapses the whole karst of descendants below its sponsors: settlement walks the tree and burns every bond in that subtree. A farm seeding N clones under shared sponsors risks N ivory bonds at once, so capital exposure grows with subtree volume as O(n), far above path-only slashing's O(log n). Clones cannot re-parent to flee, and spreading under N honest sponsors needs N outsiders each willing to watch their own harbor burn.
